title: Manos: The Hands of Fate

evidence.note: Wikipedia says the film was thought to be in the public domain, but the discovery of a copyrighted screenplay left its legal status uncertain. The print's status turns on whether the 1966 release carried a valid copyright notice. Under the pre-1978 rules, a release without a notice would generally be in the public domain, and a release with one would be protected for 95 years from publication. I found no primary source on the notice question: no film frame, Copyright Office record, Catalog of Copyright Entries (CCE) entry, or court or archive document. The notice question is unresolved, so the layer stays undetermined. The screenplay is a separate question from the film's notice.

editorial:
Manos: The Hands of Fate is a 1966 Texas horror film directed by Harold P. Warren. It premiered on November 15, 1966, at the Capri Theater in El Paso as a benefit for the local cerebral palsy fund. It reached a wide audience when Mystery Science Theater 3000 featured it in its fourth-season finale on January 30, 1993. A creator would want it for that cult fame.

The print is often called public domain, but I could not confirm that against a primary record, so no layer here is marked verified. The deciding fact is whether the 1966 release carried a copyright notice, and that is unresolved. Renewal is automatic for 1964-1977 works, so it is not the issue. The screenplay is a separate question: Wikipedia says a copyrighted screenplay was discovered, which left the film's legal status uncertain. I did not confirm whether it was registered or who owns it. Wikipedia also says a related trademark attempt by Warren's son was abandoned in 2018. The 2015 Synapse Blu-ray was made from a 16 mm workprint found in 2011, and I did not confirm what it adds. Use a plain archive.org copy rather than a disc rip, and check the notice, script and score before any commercial use.

It is often described as public domain, but a copyrighted screenplay was discovered and that left its legal status uncertain. Check the Copyright Office records for the screenplay before relying on it, and use an archive.org copy rather than a Blu-ray rip.

Not safely. Anything the 2015 Synapse release adds, such as new titles or other material, may be protected on its own, and I did not confirm what it adds. Use a copy that has not been altered.
